parts.prompt: Why can't it start with 200 GPUs and grow?
options: synchronous training needs all ranks at once

problems.title: Fragmentation
problems.statement: 1,000 8-GPU nodes; 900 GPUs are free, spread as 1 free GPU on each of 900 nodes.
problems.solution: Plenty of free GPUs, no usable gang. Bin-pack small jobs.

problems.title: Checkpoint interval
problems.statement: Checkpoint takes 5 minutes; MTBF of the job is 10 hours.

parts.prompt: Young/Daly interval √(2 × C × MTBF) in minutes?

problems.title: Failures at scale
problems.statement: Each GPU has a 0.1% chance of failing per day; a job uses 2,048 GPUs.

parts.prompt: Probability of at least one failure per day (%)?

problems.title: Backfill
problems.statement: A big job's reservation starts in 6 hours; a small job needs 8 GPUs for 4 hours.

parts.prompt: Can it backfill into the reserved nodes?
options: Yes: it finishes before the reservation
No: it would delay the reservation

problems.title: Topology
problems.statement: A TP-8 job placed across 8 different nodes instead of one node.

options: much slower: per-layer all-reduces go over the network instead of NVLink

problems.solution: Topology-aware placement keeps TP groups inside nodes.

problems.title: Async checkpoint
problems.statement: 1 TB of state; shared storage writes at 10 GB/s; copying the state to host RAM takes 20 s; checkpoints every 60 minutes.

parts.prompt: Training pause per checkpoint with synchronous writes (s)?
Pause with async (snapshot to host, write in background) (s)?

hints: Sync: bytes / storage bandwidth. Async: only the snapshot blocks.
problems.solution: 100 s vs 20 s per checkpoint; 24 checkpoints a day saves 32 minutes of cluster time, and enables more frequent checkpoints (less work lost per failure).
